title: Lamb, red cabbage and apple stew

grandparents_cupboard.reason: Everything is a kitchen staple, and chicken stock counts as good stock.

supermarket.reason: Lamb mince, red cabbage, apples and potatoes are all everyday Tesco items at normal prices.

basic_kitchen.reason: It needs only a lidded casserole, a knife and a board, and the technique is simple browning and simmering.

works.reason: 500g lamb, half a cabbage, 600g potatoes and 500ml stock make a sensible stew for four, and cubed potatoes will be tender after 40 minutes' covered simmering.

honest_times.reason: Thirty minutes covers shredding the cabbage, chopping the onion and garlic, cubing the apples and potatoes and about 13 minutes of browning, and the 40-minute cook matches the simmer.

honest_ingredients.reason: Every listed ingredient and seasoning, including the fresh thyme and cinnamon, is used in the steps, and nothing unlisted appears apart from water.

seasonal_feel.reason: A warming red cabbage and apple stew suits mid-November, and the cabbage is central to the dish.

plain_voice.reason: The steps are short and clear in plain British English, with no restaurant language or preaching.

hearty_healthy.reason: It is a filling one-pot meal of meat, vegetables, fruit and potatoes that a family would happily eat.
